executive_summary: Recent CISA alerts highlight critical auth bypasses, command injection, and race conditions across Linux, cloud, and web platforms. Focus on OpenSSH, GPUStack, WordPress, Barracuda, and Chromium for hands‑on lab practice.

signals.title: OpenBSD OpenSSH authentication bypass (Linux)
signals.what_changed: Unexpected status code in SSH protocol flow allowing auth bypass.
signals.why_it_matters: Attackers can log in without credentials, compromising remote servers.
signals.application: Build a lab OpenSSH server, apply a vulnerable version, and verify bypass with crafted packets; document detection and mitigation.

signals.title: GPUStack unauthenticated administrative access
signals.why_it_matters: Full compromise of inference clusters, secret leakage, and code execution.
signals.application: Deploy GPUStack in a container, send unauthenticated admin request, observe API‑key creation and secret disclosure; write a detection script.

signals.title: WordPress Core TOCTOU race condition RCE
signals.what_changed: Predictable staging paths during core upgrades enable unauthenticated RCE.
signals.why_it_matters: Attackers can execute code on the server during the upgrade window.
signals.application: Spin up a WP test site, simulate upgrade race, craft malicious upgrade package, verify code execution; produce a proof‑of‑concept report.

signals.title: Barracuda Networks OS command injection via timezone
signals.what_changed: Crafted timezone value triggers root‑privileged command execution.
signals.why_it_matters: Authenticated admin can run arbitrary commands with root privileges.
signals.application: Run a Barracuda ESG VM (or a simulated service), inject a malicious timezone, confirm command execution, and document detection.

signals.title: Google Chromium XML use‑after‑free sandbox bypass
signals.what_changed: Use‑after‑free in XML component allows sandbox escape via crafted webpage.
signals.why_it_matters: Arbitrary code execution in browsers that use Chromium engine.
signals.application: Set up a Chromium sandbox environment, craft malicious HTML/XML, test with sandboxie, and analyze exploit behavior.

experiment.title: Reproduce GPUStack unauthenticated admin access in a lab container
experiment.objective: Demonstrate how missing authentication on GPUStack can be abused to gain administrative control and expose secrets.
steps: Build container image with docker build .
Send POST /v2/inference‑backends/from‑yaml without authentication using curl or Python script
Check for created admin API key and any secret leakage in logs
Document findings and create a detection rule
expected_evidence: Admin API key printed in response or logs
Secrets (e.g., cloud provider keys) visible in container output
Successful creation of inference backend without auth
experiment.stop_condition: Experiment stops when admin API key is created without authentication or after 5 minutes if no unauthorized access is achieved.

discarded: Unused items not selected for signals.
